description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian curry renowned for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered in a luscious gravy, offering a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy flavors. This iconic dish promises a comforting and unforgettable culinary experience that's a staple in Indian households and restaurants worldwide.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: Cut chicken into bite-sized pieces. In a large bowl, combine yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, and lemon juice. Add chicken, mix well to coat, and marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or preferably 2-4 hours in the refrigerator for deeper flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon ghee or oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer (cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding) and cook until browned and partially cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Makhani Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add 1 tablespoon more ghee if needed. Add chopped onions and cook over medium heat until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Drain the soaked cashews and add them to the pan.

instructions.title: Build the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, remaining 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/4 teaspoon turmeric, 1 teaspoon cumin powder, and 1 teaspoon coriander powder to the pan. Season with salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until the tomatoes break down, the mixture thickens, and oil begins to separate from the sides. This step is crucial for flavor development.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the pan from heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Carefully transfer the tomato-onion-cashew mixture to a blender. Add about 1/4 cup of water if necessary to aid blending. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra silky restaurant-style gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, pressing down on solids to extract all liquid.

instructions.title: Combine and Simmer
instructions.text: Return the sieved gravy to the pot over medium heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces. If the gravy is too thick, add a splash of water to reach desired consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to finish cooking through.

instructions.title: Finish with Cream and Butter
instructions.text: Stir in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, the optional sugar or honey, and the crushed kasuri methi. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and the remaining 2 tablespoons of unsalted butter until melted and fully incorporated. Do not boil the curry vigorously after adding cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Garnish your classic Butter Chicken with fresh chopped cilantro and an optional swirl of extra cream. Serve hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fragrant basmati rice for an authentic and satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For an extra smoky flavor, char the chicken pieces lightly on a grill or under a broiler before adding to the gravy.
Soaking cashews is crucial for a smooth and rich gravy; you can substitute with blanched almonds for a similar effect.
Always add cream and butter at the very end and avoid boiling the curry vigorously afterwards to prevent curdling and maintain the velvety texture.
article:
Butter Chicken, also known as Murgh Makhani, stands as a crowning jewel in the vast repertoire of Indian cuisine. Its rich, creamy texture, subtly sweet and tangy tomato-based gravy, and succulent pieces of marinated chicken have captivated food lovers worldwide. This iconic dish is not just a meal; it's an experience, a symphony of flavors that evokes comfort and culinary delight. If you've ever yearned to recreate that authentic Indian restaurant magic in your own kitchen, understanding the nuances of Murgh Makhani is your first step.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

At its heart, Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani) is a classic Indian curry originating from Delhi in the 1950s. Credited to the Moti Mahal restaurant, it was reportedly created by accident or as a resourceful way to use leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato gravy. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," perfectly encapsulating its essence. It's characterized by tender pieces of chicken (often tandoori-style or pan-fried) swimming in a luxurious, vibrant orange-red sauce. This sauce is a masterful blend of pureed tomatoes, fresh cream, butter, and a delicate balance of aromatic spices like garam masala and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Unlike many spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken is celebrated for its mild heat and profound depth of flavor, making it incredibly appealing to a broad palate. Its widespread popularity has made it a staple in Indian restaurants globally and a beloved dish for home cooks seeking a taste of India.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting truly authentic Butter Chicken requires attention to a few key ingredients, divided into the chicken marinade and the rich, flavorful sauce.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   **Chicken:** 1.5 - 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces. Thighs are recommended for tenderness.
*   **Plain Yogurt:** 1/2 cup, full-fat for best results.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Spices:** 1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color), 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon salt.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1 tablespoon.

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   **Butter:** 4-6 tablespoons (unsalted, high quality).
*   **Oil:** 1 tablespoon (neutral oil like canola or vegetable).
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped or pureed.
*   **Ginger-Garlic Paste:** 1 tablespoon.
*   **Tomatoes:** 1 (28-ounce) can crushed tomatoes or 4-5 large fresh tomatoes, pureed.
*   **Cashews:** 1/4 cup, soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes (for richness and thickness).
*   **Spices:** 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala.
*   **Fenugreek Leaves (Kasoori Methi):** 1 tablespoon, crushed between palms. This is a crucial flavor component.
*   **Sugar:** 1-2 teaspoons (to balance acidity of tomatoes).
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Heavy Cream:** 1/2 cup (or more, to taste).
*   **Water:** 1/2 - 1 cup, as needed for desired consistency.
*   **Optional:** 1-2 green chilies, slit (for a touch of heat, remove before blending if desired).

## How to Make Classic Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step

Making classic Butter Chicken at home is surprisingly straightforward, especially when broken down into manageable steps.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat every piece. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side, developing a slight char. You can also grill or bake the chicken if preferred. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan (or a clean pot), melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and optional green chilies, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** Stir in the crushed or pureed tomatoes, soaked cashews (drained), red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt. Mix well. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the oil starts to separate.

5.  **Blend the Sauce:** Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth. For an extra silky sauce, you can pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing down on any solids.

6.  **Finish the Murgh Makhani Sauce:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over medium-low heat. Add the remaining 2-4 tablespoons of butter, garam masala, crushed kasoori methi, and sugar. Stir well until the butter melts and is fully incorporated. Simmer for 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully.

7.  **Combine and Serve:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering sauce. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Pour in the heavy cream and a little water if the sauce is too thick. Heat through for another 2-3 minutes, but do not boil after adding the cream. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is within reach with a few expert tips:

*   **Chicken Thighs are Key:** While chicken breast can be used, chicken thighs stay significantly more tender and moist in the rich sauce, resisting drying out.
*   **Marination Time:** Don't skimp on marinating the chicken. A longer marination (4 hours to overnight) allows the flavors to penetrate deeply, resulting in incredibly flavorful and tender chicken.
*   **Blend for Silkiness:** A truly smooth sauce is a hallmark of authentic Butter Chicken. Invest in a good blender and blend the sauce thoroughly. Straining it through a sieve after blending will remove any remaining fibrous bits for an ultra-luxurious texture.
*   **Kashmiri Chili Powder:** Use Kashmiri chili powder for the marinade and sauce. It imparts a beautiful, vibrant red color without adding excessive heat.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Essential:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) provide a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is absolutely crucial to the authentic taste of Murgh Makhani. Gently toast them in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing and adding to enhance their aroma.
*   **Balance Flavors:** The sauce should be a harmonious balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Adjust sugar to cut the acidity of the tomatoes and add a touch of salt at the end.
*   **Good Quality Butter and Cream:** Since these are core ingredients, their quality significantly impacts the final taste and richness of your Butter Chicken.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments, turning a simple meal into a feast.

*   **Rice:** The most classic pairing is fluffy basmati rice. Its delicate aroma and separate grains are perfect for soaking up the rich, creamy sauce. Jeera rice (cumin rice) also makes an excellent choice.
*   **Bread:** Warm, soft naan bread is indispensable for scooping up every last drop of the luscious gravy. Garlic naan, butter naan, or even plain roti or paratha are fantastic alternatives.
*   **Accompaniments:** A simple side salad of sliced cucumbers, onions, and tomatoes can provide a refreshing contrast. A dollop of cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) or a wedge of lemon can also brighten the flavors.
*   **Garnish:** Always finish your Butter Chicken with a generous sprinkling of fresh, chopped coriander leaves and, for an extra touch of indulgence, a swirl of fresh cream or a knob of butter.

## Variations and Substitutions for Murgh Makhani

While the classic Murgh Makhani is a beloved standard, its adaptable nature allows for several delicious variations and substitutions.

*   **Vegetarian Options:** For those avoiding meat, the sauce base of Butter Chicken is incredibly versatile.
    *   **Paneer Makhani:** Substitute chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese), adding them towards the end to heat through.
    *   **Tofu Makhani:** Firm or extra-firm tofu, pressed and pan-fried, can be used.
    *   **Vegetable Makhani:** A medley of vegetables like cauliflower, peas, carrots, and potatoes can be simmered in the sauce.
*   **Healthier Twist:** To reduce richness, you can use less butter and cream. Greek yogurt can be used in the marinade for added tang and protein. Instead of pan-frying, bake or grill the chicken to minimize oil. A splash of milk can replace some of the cream for a lighter sauce.
*   **Spice Level Adjustment:** For more heat, add extra green chilies or a pinch of cayenne pepper to the sauce. For less heat, omit the green chilies and use a milder red chili powder.
*   **Nut-Free Version:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. To maintain thickness, a small amount of cornstarch slurry (1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water) can be stirred into the simmering sauce.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic tandoori-like smoky flavor without a tandoor, you can employ the "dhungar" method: place a small heat-proof bowl in the pot, put a hot charcoal piece in it, drizzle a little oil or ghee over the charcoal, and quickly cover the pot for a few minutes. Alternatively, a pinch of smoked paprika can add a subtle smoky note.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's a culinary journey that promises warmth, comfort, and an explosion of delightful flavors. Whether you stick to the classic recipe or experiment with these variations, mastering Murgh Makhani will undoubtedly earn you rave reviews in your kitchen.
